dedupe_keys.name: global dam watch gdw consensus global database of river barriers and reservoirs

description: The Global Dam Watch consensus database is a harmonised global inventory of river barriers and reservoirs. Version 1 contains 41,145 barrier locations and 35,295 associated reservoir polygons with a cumulative storage capacity of 7,405 cubic kilometres and 302,450 square kilometres of artificial surface water. The GDW consortium built it to give large-scale analyses one globally consistent source: it integrates and quality-controls the three foundational datasets GOODD, GRanD and FHReD, adds 6,113 barriers from the Global River Obstruction Database and 1,451 reservoirs from the JRC Global Surface Water dataset, and co-registers every barrier and reservoir to the HydroSHEDS drainage network and RiverATLAS, with each reservoir also part of HydroLAKES 1.1. Coverage is global; the data are a snapshot of barriers and reservoirs at compilation, described by Lehner et al. in Scientific Data (8 October 2024). The database is downloadable in GIS formats and viewable online from the Global Dam Watch site, free under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: attribute completeness varies with the source dataset, small barriers are under-represented outside the obstruction sources, and GOODD and GRanD are discontinued as separate products in its favour. Simulation uses: system description of dams for flood-defence and water-supply models, reservoir storage and river-network routing, hazard exposure downstream of dams and climate adaptation studies. It supersedes GRanD (data-grand-global-reservoir-and-dam-database) and shares the HydroSHEDS framework with HydroWASTE (data-hydrowaste).
